importantNotes: Galatians is sometimes called 'Luther's book' — it was central to the Reformation.
The fruit of the Spirit (5:22-23) vs. the works of the flesh (5:19-21) — a clear contrast.
'I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live' (2:20) — the Christian's identity.
Galatians and Romans together form the theological backbone of Protestant Christianity.
Paul publicly rebuked Peter for hypocrisy regarding Gentile fellowship (2:11-14).

chapters.1: Only one gospel; Paul received his message directly from Christ, not from men.
chapters.2: Paul's gospel accepted by the Jerusalem apostles; Paul confronts Peter's hypocrisy.
chapters.3: Justified by faith, not law — Abraham believed and was credited with righteousness.
chapters.4: No longer slaves but sons and heirs; the allegory of Hagar and Sarah.
chapters.5: Stand firm in freedom; walk by the Spirit; the fruit of the Spirit vs. works of the flesh.
chapters.6: Bear one another's burdens; sow to the Spirit; boast only in the cross of Christ.
